resources.string: Maps hardware keys to custom functions
SideKeys intercepts the hardware side keys and runs the actions you choose (e.g. Google Assistant, Google Wallet or launching an app). The service does not read screen content and collects no data.

To remap the side keys, SideKeys must be enabled as an accessibility service. For apps installed from an APK, Android takes three steps — in this order, because the permission to unblock only appears *after* a blocked attempt:
Step 1: Try to switch it on
Opens accessibility settings. Tap "SideKeys Button Mapper" and try the switch — Android will refuse with "Restricted setting". That refusal is what unlocks step 2, so it is expected.
Opens the app info screen. There: menu (⋮) top right → "Allow restricted settings". This entry only exists once step 1 has been refused.
Use this if the service was working and stopped after the app was "closed" in the task manager. Only shown because SideKeys holds the permission to do it.
Restart did not work — please use step 2 and toggle SideKeys off and on.
No key assigned yet. Tap "Assign key" and then press one of your phone\'s hardware keys.
The mapping for "%1$s" will be removed. The key gets its original function back.
Now press the side key you want to assign
Works with extra side keys, volume keys and most other hardware keys.
Note: capturing already works now, but for the key to react system-wide the accessibility service must be enabled.
Choose an action for each press type. Use ▶ to test the action immediately.
Service not active — please enable the accessibility service first.
For special functions, e.g. Bigme-specific settings. Provide at least an action or a component.
Note: if a double press is assigned, the single press only fires after this window has passed.
Some side keys bounce and fire twice. Presses arriving faster than this interval are ignored.

Recommended on Bigme devices: the task manager force-stops apps that are swiped away or "closed", which kills the key service until it is toggled again. Hidden from recents, SideKeys can\'t be closed that way. Open it from the app drawer instead.

• Keys stopped working after "closing" the app? Some task managers (e.g. on Bigme devices) force-stop the app and with it the key service. Fix: toggle SideKeys off and on again in Accessibility settings. Keep "Hide from recent apps" on to prevent it.

• If a side key never arrives, the firmware may be handling it itself. On Bigme devices: set that key to "None" under Settings → "Custom key" so SideKeys receives it.

• MediaTek's "DuraSpeed" (found on Bigme and other devices) aggressively kills background apps. If the service stops, disable DuraSpeed (via ADB: settings put global setting.duraspeed.enabled 0) and exempt SideKeys from battery optimization.
Pick one of the app\'s screens (activities), or type a component below — e.g. com.openai.chatgpt/com.openai.voice.VoiceModeActivity. Screens marked as internal cannot be opened by other apps.
Could not start that screen. The app does not allow other apps to open it.
Give keys different actions while a specific app is in the foreground. Slots you leave empty fall back to the global mapping.
No app profiles yet. Tap "+ Add app" and pick the app.
No keys assigned for this app yet.
Remove all mappings for this app
Android has no API for this, so these two extras need one permission that only a privileged shell can grant. Pick either route — both are one-time, local, and read no screen content.
Shizuku is not running. Install and start the Shizuku app, or use route 2 below.
Once granted it stays until you uninstall the app — and then it also works when Shizuku is not running. Everything else in SideKeys works without it.
✓ Set up — the Battery Saver key action, the quick tile and the one-tap enable are active.
Needs the one-time adb setup — see Battery & charge alarm.
Works on any device (no root, no extra permission). When plugged in and this level is reached, SideKeys plays a sound, vibrates and shows a notification so you can unplug.
Battery reached %1$d%% — unplug to protect it.
No assistant found. Is the Google Assistant installed?
App not found — has it been uninstalled?
This action requires Android 9 or newer.
No flashlight found on this device.
The action could not be executed.
Please allow SideKeys to access Do Not Disturb and try again.
Battery Saver tile in Quick Settings

SideKeys can register its tile even where the panel hides the "edit tiles" button. Note for Bigme devices: they ship a modified SystemUI whose panel draws its own fixed set of tiles (Power Management, E Ink Center, Full refresh) and never reads the system tile list, so a tile added here cannot become visible — confirmed on the HiBreak Pro. Map Battery Saver to a key instead.
The tile is in the panel\'s tile list. Pull the shade down twice to check — if it isn\'t visible, this firmware ignores the list.

✓ The system registered the tile. If it still does not appear in the panel, this firmware draws its own fixed set of tiles and ignores registered ones — nothing an app can change. Use the key action instead.
Nothing else in the app depends on the tile — mapping Battery Saver to a key always works, and is the reliable route on firmwares with a custom panel.
You declined the system dialog. Tap again to retry.
This firmware has no add-tile dialog, and Android 14 only lets a privileged shell edit the tile list. Start Shizuku and tap again — or run this from a computer:
Could not write the tile list.
Written to the tile list, but the system did not confirm adding it. Pull the shade down twice — if the tile isn\'t there, this panel does not read the list.
The tile is in the list at position %1$d — that is likely on a later page of the panel. Swipe sideways in the tile area, or move it to the front:
Move SideKeys tile to the front
Move the built-in Battery Saver tile to the front
Moved. Pull the shade down twice — "Battery Saver" should now be on the first page.
Step 3: Switch it on for real
Back to accessibility settings — the switch for "SideKeys Button Mapper" now works.
